title: Dodgers Shut Down Shohei Ohtani From Pitching Indefinitely Over Lingering Knee Injury
excerpt: The four-time MVP will continue to hit but has no timetable for returning to the mound after treatment failed to resolve his left knee discomfort.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Shohei Ohtani's pitching is indefinitely shut down due to a persistent knee injury.
  • Ohtani last pitched on July 3 and has not improved despite treatment.
  • He will continue to hit for the Dodgers while recovering.
  • The Dodgers lead the NL West by 11½ games, allowing cautious management of Ohtani's injury.

Shohei Ohtani's pitching season is on hold indefinitely after the Los Angeles Dodgers announced Sunday that the two-way superstar will not return to the mound until his lingering left knee injury shows meaningful improvement.

Manager Dave Roberts told reporters in Philadelphia that Ohtani's scheduled start against the Phillies on Wednesday has been scrapped, and there is no timeline for when he might pitch again. "It's going to be some time" before Ohtani is back on the bump, Roberts said.

A Knee That Won't Cooperate

Ohtani last pitched on July 3, and the left knee discomfort that sidelined him has proven stubborn. He skipped the All-Star Game in Philadelphia — where he was voted in as a starter — to receive a lubricant injection aimed at reducing the irritation. But Roberts acknowledged the treatment has not produced the desired results.

> **"Sure," Roberts said of the possibility Ohtani could pitch through the discomfort."**

"Sure," Roberts said of the possibility Ohtani could pitch through the discomfort."

https://x.com/UnderdogMLB/status/2078880305847341330

"His knee, we just want to continue to give it the best chance to kind of get into a good spot. It's the pitching and the torque of landing on that leg that kind of gets it upset."

— Dave Roberts, Dodgers manager

Roberts clarified that the injury is not worsening but has simply "not gotten better," and that the decision to shut Ohtani down is precautionary rather than reactive. The knee does not bother him while batting, which is why he will remain in the lineup as the designated hitter.

According to Sportsnet's report from Philadelphia, Ohtani is expected to throw off a mound sometime later this week — potentially Thursday or Friday — as a preliminary step. The Dodgers visit the White House on Thursday before beginning a three-game series at the New York Mets on Friday.

Ohtani's Injury Timeline

Ohtani last pitched due to left knee irritation.

Upcoming (August 2023)
Expected to throw off a mound as a preliminary step.

Impact on the Dodgers' Season

The two-time defending World Series champions hold the best record in baseball at 63-37 and command an 11½-game lead in the NL West, giving them the luxury of caution. But losing Ohtani's arm — he had been pitching at an elite level before the injury, putting himself in Cy Young Award conversations — strips the rotation of its most dynamic weapon during the second-half push toward October.

"Could he probably do it? Sure," Roberts said of the possibility Ohtani could pitch through the discomfort. "But right now, the benefits just don't seem to outweigh the cost at this time of the season. I think we still have plenty of time to get him to a good spot."

Ohtani's Historic Two-Way Campaign

The shutdown dims what had been shaping up as another historic two-way season for Ohtani. The 32-year-old, who signed a record 10-year, $700 million contract with the Dodgers before the 2024 season, returned to pitching in 2025 after Tommy John surgery and had been increasingly effective on the mound this year.

Cy Young Candidacy Impacted

His Cy Young candidacy is now effectively over, according to Sporting News, though he remains one of the most productive hitters in baseball from the left side. The Dodgers' priority is clear: keep Ohtani healthy for what they hope will be a third consecutive championship run.

Roberts would not put a specific date on Ohtani's return. "He's got to play catch again and then we'll see," he said. For a team built around its generational talent, patience is the only strategy that makes sense.
